description: UI Bridge State Machine page — connect to SDK-integrated apps, discover UI states via automated exploration or manual recording with fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis, then manage state machine configs across seven tabs: Discovery (SDK app connection, explore/record data collection, fingerprint-based state discovery with auto-save), Graph Editor (interactive dagre node-edge layout with element thumbnails, drag-and-drop element reassignment, transition creation), State View (list + spatial + screenshot modes via shared StateViewPanel), Transitions (list with action playback via shared TransitionsPanel), Pathfinding (find optimal paths between states via shared PathfindingPanel), Exploration Results (dashboard with pass rate, coverage stats, discrepancy severity groups, history list, and per-state detail with confidence scores, element verification, and AI analysis prompt), and Export (save to JSON file or load into Python runtime).

groups.description: The state discovery algorithm uses fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis to group UI elements into states. Co-occurrence data is collected via exploration (automated interaction) or recording (manual capture). Each capture produces a fingerprint of visible interactive elements. States are discovered by clustering fingerprints with similar element sets. The algorithm correctness can be verified by examining the discovered states' element lists and confidence scores.

groups.description: The state machine follows the multistate model (qontinui/multistate), which extends model-based GUI automation theory. These rules define how states, elements, and screenshots relate to each other. The multistate formal model is Ω = (S, T, G, ω, Td) where S is the set of states, T the transitions, G state groups, ω the occlusion function, and Td dynamic transition generation. All state machine features — discovery, graph editing, state view, screenshots, and export — must conform to these rules. Source: https://qontinui.github.io/multistate/
groups.name: State Model Rules (qontinui/multistate)

groups.description: Co-occurrence observations drive state element lists via a derive → promote → invalidate → undo loop. The page surface exposes this via ObservationsPanel (mounted below the page header) and ProvenanceBadge (rendered next to each state name in the detail panel). ObservationsPanel shows the most recent drift fit_score (from GET /state-discovery/drift-scores), offers a 'Re-derive all' bulk action (POST /state-discovery/derive?window_days=90), an 'Invalidate spec observations' button (POST /co-occurrence/invalidate — disabled with tooltip when the StateMachineConfig has no spec_id), and an invalidation log table fed by GET /co-occurrence/invalidations. Each invalidation is grouped by undo_token; rows within the 24 h window show an Undo button (POST /co-occurrence/invalidate/undo). ProvenanceBadge renders three variants — green 'observed' (with support/contrast tooltip + observation count + age), gray 'ai-generated', yellow 'ai-fallback' (with invalidation age). Missing provenance on older compiled SMs silently falls back to 'ai-generated'.
groups.name: Observation Pipeline Surface

states.description: The page header shows a Network icon, the active config name (or 'UI Bridge States' when none is selected), and a config selector dropdown with a Refresh button. Users pick an existing config to load it. There is no 'New' or 'Delete' button — configs are created through the Discovery flow.
states.name: Page Header and Config Selector

states.description: Seven tabs appear below the header and are always visible (regardless of config selection): Discovery, Graph Editor, State View, Transitions, Pathfinding, Exploration Results, and Export. The active tab is highlighted with a background shadow. Each tab has an icon and label.
states.name: Tab Navigation Bar

states.description: When no config is selected, most tabs show centered placeholder text guiding the user. Discovery and Exploration Results tabs are always available regardless of config selection.

elements.textContent: Select a configuration to view the state graph
Select a configuration to view states
Select a configuration to view transitions
Select a configuration to use pathfinding

states.name: Empty States (No Config Selected)

states.description: Phase 1 of the Discovery flow. Users scan for SDK-integrated apps (web and desktop), see discovered apps in a list, and connect to one. Once connected, a green 'Connected: [AppName]' banner appears and the app list hides. Auto-scans on mount.

elements.textContent: Click Scan to find apps with the UI Bridge SDK installed.

states.name: Discovery Tab: Connect to SDK App

states.description: Phase 2 of Discovery. After connecting to an app, two sub-tabs appear: 'Explore' (automated exploration) and 'Record' (manual capture session). Explore automatically interacts with UI elements; Record lets users manually navigate while capturing states. Both produce co-occurrence data for state discovery.
states.name: Discovery Tab: Data Collection (Explore/Record)

states.description: Phase 3-4 of Discovery. After co-occurrence data is collected, the connection card hides and a data summary card appears. Users click 'Discover States' to run fingerprint-based state discovery. Results show discovered states with confidence scores. After auto-save or manual save with a config name, the user is redirected to the Graph Editor tab.
states.name: Discovery Tab: State Discovery and Save

states.description: The Graph Editor tab renders an interactive node-edge graph using @xyflow/react with dagre layout. States are nodes and transitions are edges. A floating 'Add Transition' button is positioned at top-left. Clicking a node opens the state detail side panel; clicking an edge opens the transition editor side panel. Supports drag-and-drop element reassignment between states and transition deletion. An empty graph shows an instructional message.
states.name: Graph Editor Tab Content

states.description: The graph canvas has control buttons in the top-right (Fit, keyboard shortcut toggle, Re-layout), a MiniMap in the bottom-right, and keyboard shortcuts. Nodes display element thumbnails, badges (START, outgoing/incoming counts), and confidence indicators. Extra shortcut entries show 'Create transition: Drag element' and 'Move element: Alt+Drag'.
states.name: Graph Visualization Controls

states.description: The State View tab shows all states using the shared StateViewPanel component. It supports three view modes: List (collapsible text list), Spatial (force-directed canvas), and Screenshot (three-panel viewer with bounding box overlays). State selection syncs with the graph tab's selectedStateId. No 'Add State' button — states come from Discovery.
states.name: State View Tab Content

states.description: The Transitions tab shows all transitions using the shared TransitionsPanel component with a left sidebar (searchable transition list with state filters) and a right detail panel with action playback controls.

elements.textContent: Select a transition to view its details

states.name: Transitions Tab Content

states.description: The Pathfinding tab provides graph pathfinding between states using the shared PathfindingPanel component. Users select a 'From' and 'To' state from dropdowns, choose an algorithm (Dijkstra or BFS), and click 'Find Path'. Results show the path steps with transition names and costs. Found paths are highlighted on the graph.
states.name: Pathfinding Tab Content

states.description: When a state is selected in the Graph Editor, a w-80 side panel opens on the right showing the shared StateDetailPanel component. It provides a 'State Details' header with Close button, editable name, description, metadata grid, element list with type-colored badges, acceptance criteria list, domain knowledge cards, and save/delete actions.
states.name: Side Panel: State Detail

states.description: When a transition is selected or 'Add Transition' is clicked in the Graph Editor, a w-80 side panel opens on the right showing the shared TransitionEditor component. In create mode it shows 'New Transition' header; in edit mode it shows 'Edit Transition' header. The editor provides a Close button, name input, state toggle groups (From, Activate, Exit), action list with type-specific fields, path cost, and stays-visible checkbox.
states.name: Side Panel: Transition Editor

states.description: The Exploration Results tab shows a summary dashboard with pass rate, state coverage, transition coverage, discrepancy counts by severity, and recent exploration runs. View mode toggles allow switching between Dashboard and History views. An AI Analysis button is shown (disabled until a run is selected). The tab uses off-screen positioning instead of display:none so that UI Bridge SDK can still scan severity elements when the tab is inactive.
states.name: Exploration Results: Summary Dashboard

states.description: The dashboard displays discrepancy counts grouped by severity in a 3-column grid: Critical (red, XCircle icon), Warning (amber, AlertTriangle icon), and Info (blue, Info icon). Each severity group has a data-testid attribute for automated testing. A role='list' with aria-label='discrepancy severity groups critical warning info' wraps the groups.
states.name: Exploration Results: Discrepancy Severity Groups

states.description: The dashboard shows recent exploration runs (up to 5) and the History view shows all runs. Each run row displays a status badge (Passed/Failed/Unknown), config name, strategy badge (color-coded), timestamp, summary text, and run ID. Clicking a run navigates to the detail view.
states.name: Exploration Results: History and Run List

states.description: When a run is selected, the detail view shows the report header (config name, strategy badge, timestamp), summary stats grid (Pass Rate, States, Transitions, Discrepancies), discrepancies by severity, expandable state detail cards with confidence scores and element verification, and an AI Analysis prompt button.
states.name: Exploration Results: Detail View

states.description: The Export tab provides a centered panel with a FileJson icon heading, description text about JSON export compatible with UIBridgeRuntime.from_dict(), config summary (name, state count, transition count), and two action buttons: 'Save to File' (Tauri save dialog) and 'Load into Runtime' (POST to /state-machine/load). Both show spinners during operation.
states.name: Export Tab

states.description: The state discovery algorithm uses fingerprint-based co-occurrence analysis to group UI elements into states. Co-occurrence data is collected via exploration (automated interaction) or recording (manual capture). Each capture produces a fingerprint of visible interactive elements. States are discovered by clustering fingerprints with similar element sets. The algorithm correctness can be verified by examining the discovered states' element lists and confidence scores.
states.name: Discovery Algorithm: Fingerprint-Based State Grouping

states.description: The state machine follows the multistate model (qontinui/multistate), which extends model-based GUI automation theory. These rules define how states, elements, and screenshots relate to each other. The multistate formal model is Ω = (S, T, G, ω, Td) where S is the set of states, T the transitions, G state groups, ω the occlusion function, and Td dynamic transition generation. All state machine features — discovery, graph editing, state view, screenshots, and export — must conform to these rules. Source: https://qontinui.github.io/multistate/
states.name: State Model Rules (qontinui/multistate)
